title: `Prepare` memvalidasi foto SEBELUM PIN
check: REPEATING = the diff moves PIN verification ahead of the outlet photo policy check / full image decode in Prepare, or relocates image validation into the (non-fatal) save step so any non-empty photo string satisfies the "photo required" policy.
reply:
Tidak ada edit yang saya buat. Alasannya dua, dan keduanya terukur.

## 1. Urutannya sudah seperti yang Anda minta

PIN dicek **sebelum** decode, di kedua arah:

| | cek kredensial | decode foto |
|---|---|---|
| `ClockIn` | `attendance.go:296` `proveSubject` | `attendance.go:310` `Prepare` |
| `ClockOut` | `attendance.go:616` `proveSubject` | `attendance.go:623` `Prepare` |

`proveSubject` memverifikasi password + PIN staf lewat `AuthService.VerifyStaffForOutlet`, dan komentarnya di `attendance.go:169` memang menyebut itu alasannya ("so a password guess never spends a call to the face sidecar").

Dan di jalur absen biasa **tidak ada PIN sama sekali** di request itu. PIN dicocokkan di `POST /api/auth/unlock`, request terpisah yang jauh lebih dulu; `attendanceRequest` hanya membawa `password`/`pin` untuk jalur "catat absen staf lain". Jadi tidak ada CPU decode yang terbuang untuk PIN salah — tidak sekarang, dan tidak ada tempat untuk memindahkannya.

## 2. Decode-nya bukan sumber lemotnya

Saya benchmark `decodeImageDataURL` langsung (file benchmark sementara, sudah dihapus, tree bersih):

```
BenchmarkDecodeImageDataURL/60KiB-10        46284 ns/op     (0,046 ms)
BenchmarkDecodeImageDataURL/2048KiB-10    1012682 ns/op     (1,01 ms)
```

60 KiB itu ukuran wajar frame webcam 480px yang dikirim terminal; 2 MiB adalah plafon `MaxSelfieBytes`, jadi 1 ms adalah kasus **terburuk** yang mungkin. Kandidat lemot yang nyata di jalur ini adalah round trip HTTP ke sidecar wajah (`face-svc`, python + ONNX) — yang sudah berdiri paling akhir justru supaya tidak terbuang — plus baca DB geofence, plus waktu kamera di sisi FE. Kalau mau, saya ukur per-gerbang di jam ramai dan laporkan angkanya.

## 3. Validasi di save time: ini yang sengaja TIDAK saya kerjakan

`Persist` memang non-fatal (`attendance.go:362` hanya `log.Warn`), dan itu keputusan sadar: blip MinIO tidak boleh mengunci kasir dari shift-nya sendiri. Konsekuensinya, kalau validasi gambar hanya terjadi di sana, satu-satunya yang benar-benar ditegakkan tinggal "field-nya string tidak kosong". Ini sudah pernah terjadi: `data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2Zy8+` ditolak decoder tapi request-nya tetap dijawab **200** di outlet yang `selfie_required` — "wajib foto" hilang tanpa satu pun error. Kasusnya terkunci di `attendance_photo_service_test.go:65`.

Ada alasan kedua yang lebih keras: `runFaceGate` menerima `selfie` dan membandingkan **bytes**-nya. Foto harus sudah terdekode sebelum gerbang wajah jalan, jadi menunda decode ke waktu simpan berarti mematikan verifikasi wajah, bukan sekadar menggeser validasi.

**CHANGES MADE:** tidak ada.

**THINGS I DIDN'T TOUCH:** `backend/internal/service/attendance_photo_service.go` dan `backend/internal/handler/attendance.go` — urutan yang diminta sudah berlaku, dan memindahkan validasi ke save time akan mencabut gerbang "wajib foto" plus gerbang wajah.

**POTENTIAL CONCERNS:** laporan "lemot"-nya nyata tapi belum terlokalisasi. Kalau Anda mau, saya instrumentasi `ClockIn` per-gerbang (durasi decode / geofence / sidecar) dan jalankan di outlet yang mengeluh, supaya angka yang memutuskan bukan tebakan. Dan kalau 2 MiB terasa terlalu longgar untuk wifi restoran, menurunkan `MaxSelfieBytes` adalah knob yang aman dan tidak menyentuh urutan gerbang apa pun.

Confidence: 9/10 | Risk: low
reason: No diff was produced; the developer refused to change anything and explained in detail that PIN/credential checks already precede photo decode and that moving validation into the non-fatal save step would gut both the photo-required and face gates.

title: Anggaran laba-rugi dibandingkan sebagai HARI KALENDER, bukan instan

reply:
Sudah saya periksa ujung ke ujung — dan **tidak ada yang perlu dilengkapi**: `ResolvePnLBudgets` di `backend/internal/domain/pnl_budget.go:53` sudah persis melakukan yang Anda minta, jadi saya tidak mengubah apa pun.

**Yang sudah ada di sana** (`pnl_budget.go:53-69`): untuk setiap `line_key`, ambil baris dengan `effective_from` paling baru yang **tidak lebih besar** dari hari yang diminta (`if from > on { continue }`), lalu pertahankan yang terbaru di antara kandidat (`if ok && from <= cur... { continue }`). Target yang belum mulai dilewati; target yang dicabut (`TargetBps == nil`) tetap mengembalikan PIC-nya.

Perbandingannya sengaja per **hari kalender string** (`Format("2006-01-02")`), bukan per instant — `effective_from` adalah kolom `DATE` yang di-scan sebagai tengah malam UTC, sementara hari yang dibandingkan adalah tengah malam Jakarta (tujuh jam lebih awal). Kalau dibandingkan sebagai `time.Time`, target yang mulai tanggal 1 justru tidak berlaku pada tanggal 1.

**Bukti, bukan klaim:**

```
=== RUN   TestResolvePnLBudgetsTakesTheRowInForceThatDay
--- PASS (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestResolvePnLBudgetsAppliesOnItsFirstJakartaDay
--- PASS (0.00s)
ok  github.com/kitapos/kitapos/internal/domain  1.039s
```

Dua tes itu sudah mengunci keempat kasusnya: target lebih baru menggantikan yang lama, target yang belum mulai tidak muncul, target yang dicabut menyimpan PIC, dan batas hari pertama Jakarta.

**Yang saya periksa dan sengaja tidak saya ubah:**

- **Kemungkinan dua baris dengan tanggal sama** — tidak bisa terjadi: `pnl_budgets` unik pada `(restaurant_id, line_key, effective_from)` (`pnl_budget_repo.go:93`, migrasi 198), dan `List` sudah `ORDER BY effective_from`. Jadi tie-break di fungsi itu tidak pernah terpakai; menambah aturan tie-break baru akan jadi kode mati.
- **Pemanggilnya sudah lengkap** — `pnl_monthly_service.go:128` me-resolve per bulan dengan hari pertama bulan itu, `:152` me-resolve untuk editor dengan `now` Jakarta, dan `pnl_monthly.go:230` sama. Tidak ada jalur P&L lain (harian atau mingguan) yang kehilangan target.

Satu catatan yang perlu keputusan Anda, bukan tebakan saya: kalau "tiap hari" yang Anda maksud adalah **rincian per-tanggal di dalam laporan bulanan** (satu baris per hari, masing-masing dengan target hari itu), itu belum ada — laporan bulanan sekarang satu baris per bulan dan memakai target yang berlaku di tanggal 1. Fungsi resolve-nya sudah siap menjawab hari apa pun, yang belum ada adalah surface hariannya (`PnLMonth` tidak punya field harian, dan `PnLByDateRange` dipanggil per bulan). Itu pekerjaan di service + handler + FE, di luar file yang Anda sebut, jadi saya tidak mulai sendiri. Bilang saja kalau mau saya kerjakan.

**CHANGES MADE:** tidak ada.

**THINGS I DIDN'T TOUCH:**
- `backend/internal/domain/pnl_budget.go` — sudah memenuhi spesifikasinya, teruji, hijau.
- `pnl_monthly_service.go` / `pnl_monthly.go` — pemanggil sudah benar; rincian harian belum diminta eksplisit.

Tidak ada commit, tidak ada push, tidak ada server dijalankan — sesuai permintaan.

```
--- PASS (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestResolvePnLBudgetsAppliesOnItsFirstJakartaDay
--- PASS (0.00s)
```

## Satu hal yang saya periksa khusus, dan ternyata tidak bisa terjadi

Satu-satunya celah yang masuk akal di kode seperti ini adalah **seri** — dua baris untuk line yang sama dengan `effective_from` identik, yang akan membuat hasilnya bergantung urutan. Itu mustahil di sini: `pnl_budget_repo.go:93` ber-`ON CONFLICT (restaurant_id, line_key, effective_from)`, jadi ada unique constraint yang membuat pasangan itu cuma bisa satu baris. Dan `List` sudah `ORDER BY b.effective_from` naik.

Pemanggilnya juga sudah konsisten mengirim hari dalam zona Jakarta — `pnl_monthly_service.go:128` (awal bulan) dan `:152` (hari ini), `pnl_monthly.go:230` (`time.Now().In(jakartaLoc)`) — jadi kontrak "hari kalender Jakarta" yang diasumsikan resolver memang dipenuhi.

title: Basis invoice platform: `o.paid_at IS NOT NULL` bukan status, `DISTINCT o.id`
check: REPEATING = the platform basis query filters on o.status instead of `o.paid_at IS NOT NULL`, or drops `DISTINCT o.id` so split-payment bills contribute their subtotal more than once; also counts if `platformFeeBillableOutlet` / `platformFeeNettedOrder` clauses are dropped in the rewrite.
reply:
## BUILDING: basis biaya platform lebih kebaca — DISTINCT dilepas, filter status DITOLAK

Satu dari dua perubahan dikerjakan. Yang satu lagi tidak, dan ini alasannya.

### Yang tidak dikerjakan: filter `o.status IN ('completed','paid')`

Tiga hal, dari yang paling murah:

1. **`paid` bukan status yang ada.** `backend/internal/domain/order.go:25-30` cuma punya `pending`/`running`/`ready`/`completed`/`cancelled`. Di DB dev: `count(*) WHERE status='paid'` = **0**. Literal itu mati sejak ditulis.
2. **Uang dan layanan dua sumbu** — `paid_at` vs `status`, dipisah migrasi 093, dan komentar di `platform_invoice_repo.go:128` sudah mengejanya: *"countsAsSale, never `o.status` (money axis, migration 093)"*. Settle menstempel `paid_at` dan **tidak** menyentuh status, jadi bon lunas tetap `pending|running|ready` selama masih di antrean kasir/KDS.
3. **Terukur di DB dev** (26.172 bon lunas) — menukar `countsAsSale("o")` dengan filter status itu:
   - memasukkan **36 bon komplimen** (Rp 770.000 subtotal) ke basis yang **ditagih** — bon yang digratiskan jadi pendapatan penuh
   - mengeluarkan **8 bon lunas-tapi-masih-berjalan** (Rp 301.000)
   - bersih **+Rp 469.000** di basis, jadi tagihan merchant berubah tanpa ada yang error

Dan **`just audit-sale-predicate` tidak menangkapnya** — gerbang itu hanya memburu `paid_at` yang ditulis tangan. Dibuktikan: saya terapkan perubahan status itu, jalankan gerbangnya, hasilnya tetap 4 pelanggaran lama dan **nol** yang menyebut `settlement_repo.go`. Jadi tidak ada apa pun yang akan menahannya kalau mendarat.

### Yang dikerjakan: DISTINCT dilepas — tapi bukan dengan join biasa

Join payments-orders tanpa DISTINCT menggandakan bon split. Di DB dev: **257 bon** punya lebih dari satu leg → **329 baris ekstra**, **Rp 36.629.000** basis palsu, plus jumlah bon membengkak (yang juga merusak tarif tetap per-pesanan). Lengan join-biasa diukur: 26.356 baris / Rp 3.316.986.000 lawan 26.066 / Rp 3.284.867.000.

Jadi DISTINCT-nya saya buang dengan menghapus **sebabnya**, bukan gejalanya — `FROM orders o` + `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id)`. Query-nya sekarang menyatakan maksudnya langsung (satu baris per bon) tanpa butuh DISTINCT untuk membereskan duplikat yang join itu sendiri bikin.

**Setara baris per baris** di DB dev: 26.066 baris kedua bentuk, selisih simetris (`EXCEPT ALL` dua arah) **0**, basis Rp 3.284.867.000 identik. Pembandingnya dibuktikan bisa membedakan lewat lengan join-biasa di atas.

### CHANGES MADE
- `backend/internal/repository/settlement_repo.go:409` — `commissionQ`: DISTINCT + join payments → `FROM orders o` + EXISTS; komentarnya ikut diperbarui.
- `backend/internal/repository/platform_invoice_repo.go:148` — `platformBasisQ` (basis invoice yang sesungguhnya) sama persis; komentarnya memang menyatakan bentuknya disalin dari settlement_repo.go, jadi mengubah satu saja membuat keduanya berpisah.
- `docs/progress.md` + `docs/changelog.md` v1.262.1, `releases_gen.go` lewat `just docs-features`.

### THINGS I DIDN'T TOUCH
- `sale_predicate.go` — pemiliknya, tidak ada alasan menyentuhnya.
- 4 pelanggaran `audit-sale-predicate` yang **sudah merah sebelum sesi ini**: `order_day_close.go:44,47`, `review_reward_redeem_repo.go:65`, `vendor_repo.go:238`. Di luar scope — mau saya beresin terpisah?

**Verifikasi:** `go build ./...` + `go vet` bersih, `go test ./internal/repository/ ./internal/domain/` ok, `just check-features` up to date, gerbang sale-predicate tetap 4 pelanggaran lama (nol baru). Tidak di-commit, tidak di-push, server tidak dijalankan.

## CHANGES MADE

- `backend/internal/faspay/types.go`: lifted the anonymous nested struct out of `CancelResponse` into a named `CancelError`. Field name, JSON tags, and `Code()` behaviour are byte-identical in effect — only construction gets easier.
- `backend/internal/faspay/adapter_test.go`: the wrapped case now reads `&CancelResponse{ResponseError: &CancelError{...}}` instead of re-declaring the anonymous struct with its tags.

## NOT DONE YET — both deliberate

**1. Production hosts: already there, and the "same pattern as sandbox" premise is wrong.**

`HostsFor("production")` already returns the production set, measured live 2026-08-23 and recorded in `p-payments.md`:

```go
XpressBaseURL: "https://xpress.faspay.co.id"          // does follow "drop -sandbox"
InquiryURL:    "https://web.faspay.co.id/cvr/100004/10" // different host entirely
```

Only checkout follows the sandbox pattern. Inquiry moves to `web.faspay.co.id` — not `debit.faspay.co.id`. And `CancelURL` is empty in production **on purpose**: Faspay doesn't publish that host, and the empty value is the signal `Adapter.CanCancel` reads to report cancel as unavailable. Had I "adjusted the host" for all three, I'd have minted `https://debit.faspay.co.id/cvr/100005/10`, flipped `CanCancel` to true in production, and had the cashier's cancel button POST real bills at a host that doesn't exist — green at every layer, as Faspay failures always are.

Nothing to add. If a production cancel host does exist now, I need the value off the merchant page; I won't derive it.

The debit host answers a cancel two ways: the flat body the docs describe (`response_code` at top level) and a `response_error` wrapper. `Code()` exists to read whichever arrived; `TestCancelOutcomeMapsDebitResponseCodes` locks both. Dropping the wrapper means a malformed cancel unmarshals to an empty `ResponseCode`, `cancelOutcome` falls through to `default`, and every error becomes an `APIError` with a blank code and blank message — the `85` "missing TRX_ID" case stops being diagnosable.

So I did the part of that ask that's actually available: the shape count is unchanged, but the awkward unmarshal target is now a named type.

- `config.go:404` still defaults `FaspayCancelURL` to the sandbox cancel host whenever `AppEnv != "production"`, while `gatewayaccount/build.go` goes through `HostsFor`. Two paths, same decision — not touched, but worth knowing they'd drift if someone edits one.

reply:
I stopped before editing. This specific change is a revert of a recorded incident fix, so I'm bringing it back to you instead of shipping it.

## What I found

**1. The skip-silently behaviour existed, and was removed on purpose.** `.claude/rules/lessons/p-lessons-backend-internal-service-procurement-service.md` records it verbatim:

> Baris non-positif pada transfer dulu dibuang diam-diam dari shipment sementara request tetap 201 (modal tertutup sebagai sukses dan sebagian kiriman tak pernah berangkat); seluruh request kini ditolak, seperti aturan tingkat-baris saudaranya.

That is exactly the behaviour requested — skip the bad line, keep the rest, answer 201. The gate that replaced it is `backend/internal/service/procurement_service.go:132-136`, and the comment on it says the same thing.

**2. The damage is physical, not cosmetic.** A stock transfer debits the sender immediately and credits the receiver only on confirmation (`domain.StockTransfer` doc comment). A silently-skipped line means the warehouse screen closes green, the destination outlet never receives that ingredient, and nothing anywhere says a line was dropped — so the shortage is found at the shelf, days later, with no record to trace. A `minus` line is the worse half: a negative qty is typed data, not an empty slot. Skipping it discards something the merchant intended to send.

**3. The premise doesn't hold for the form it blames.** `frontend/pages/hq/stock-transfer.vue:75` — `addLine()` pushes `{ ingredient_id: <first ingredient>, qty: 1 }`. A new row is already valid; a zero/blank row only exists if someone clears the field. And the form already refuses to submit it twice over (lines 86 and 137, submit disabled), so a blank row never reaches the server from that screen in the first place. "Request gagal total gara-gara satu baris kosong" would have to come from a different client.

**4. Where it would have to live anyway.** `procurement.go` is types and sentinel errors only — it holds no shipment-assembly code. The filter would land in `ProcurementService.CreateTransfer` (service) or the repository, not the file named.

## What I'd do instead

Keep the server gate, fix the form friction that actually bites:

- **Prune untouched rows at submit** — a row whose ingredient and qty were never edited is dropped client-side before the request, with a visible count ("1 baris kosong dilewati") so nothing disappears quietly.
- **Name the offending row** — `TRANSFER_LINE_QTY_INVALID` currently returns one generic sentence; return the index so the field highlights instead of the whole modal failing opaquely.

That gets you "one stray row doesn't kill the transfer" without a 201 that overstates what shipped.

If you want the skip anyway, say so and I'll build it — but I'd want it loud rather than silent: skip the line, ship the rest, still 201, and return the dropped lines in the response body so the screen can show "2 baris tidak dikirim" and `docs/qa/context.md` can carry the new invariant.


title: Baris non-positif pada transfer: seluruh request ditolak, bukan dibuang diam-diam
check: REPEATING = non-positive transfer lines are filtered/skipped while the request still succeeds, instead of the whole request being rejected with domain.ErrTransferLineQtyInvalid.
reply:
ped before editing. Here's why — the change asked for is a defect that this repo already found, fixed, and locked on both sides.

**BUILDING: skip non-positive transfer lines in `domain/procurement.go` so a shipment composes without them and still answers 201.** Not shipped — this is exactly the behaviour that was removed on purpose.

## What the evidence says

The silent-drop-plus-201 shape is a logged, high-severity finding, not an untouched default:

- `docs/audit/2026-08-24-page-wiring-findings.json` — `kind: "silent-failure"`, `severity: "high"`: *"A transfer line whose quantity field is cleared is silently dropped by the server while the request still returns 201, so the modal closes as a success and part of the shipment never leaves."*
- `docs/lessons/backend.md:589` records the fix: *"Baris non-positif pada transfer dulu dibuang diam-diam dari shipment sementara request tetap 201 … seluruh request kini ditolak, seperti aturan tingkat-baris saudaranya."*
- `backend/internal/service/procurement_service.go:128-136` carries the reason at the line that would repeat it, and the rule is deliberately the same as `ReceivePurchaseOrder`'s.
- `tests/uat/procurement/transfers/04-invalid-line-qty-refused.hurl` asserts `HTTP 400` + `TRANSFER_LINE_QTY_INVALID`, and then asserts the sender's stock is untouched. Implementing the skip means editing a committed slice whose header literally names the behaviour being asked for.

## The premise doesn't hold today

A blank row can't reach the server from the form. `frontend/pages/hq/stock-transfer.vue`:

- `addLine()` (:74) seeds `qty: 1`, never empty.
- `hasInvalidLine` (:85) catches `''`, `NaN` and `<= 0`, and `save()` (:128) refuses locally with *"Setiap baris transfer harus punya jumlah positif"* before any request goes out.
- Each row has its own remove button (`transfer-remove-line-<i>`, :407).

So "gagal total gara-gara satu baris kosong" is currently an inline form message pointing at a row you can delete, not a lost request. If someone is seeing a hard failure, the cause is somewhere else and worth diagnosing before changing the rule.

## And the inverted-sign case gets worse, not better

Your second case — qty flipped to minus — is a typo, not noise. Skipping it means a cashier meaning to send 5 kg of beef sends nothing, the modal says success, the receiving outlet confirms a shipment that never contained it, and stock on both shelves is wrong with zero errors anywhere. Refusing a shipment is recoverable in ten seconds; a shipment that silently omitted an ingredient is found days later during opname.

## Three ways forward — your call

1. **Fix the real friction in the form instead (my recommendation).** Drop genuinely *blank* rows (no ingredient chosen and qty untouched) at compose time in `save()`, keep the server's 400, and keep refusing a row where a real ingredient has qty 0 or negative. Blank-row annoyance goes away; no silent partial shipment becomes possible. No domain change, no UAT change.
2. **Skip in the domain, but make it loud.** Add `domain.PartitionTransferLines(lines) (kept, skipped []TransferLine)`, service ships `kept`, response carries the skipped rows, and the modal says "2 baris dilewati karena jumlahnya kosong" instead of plain success. Still 201. Costs: reopens the audit finding in weakened form, rewrites the UAT slice, needs a new response field in `types/api.ts` plus copy. All-lines-invalid still has to 400 (`ErrTransferLinesRequired`) or you create empty shipments.
3. **Skip silently as asked.** Service drops the guard, the UAT slice gets inverted, the FE guard comes out, and `docs/lessons/backend.md` + the audit entry get updated to say the decision was reversed. I'll do it if you confirm — but it reinstates a high-severity silent failure on stock, so I won't pick it for you.

Tell me which, and I'll implement it in one pass. I'd go with 1.

Confidence: 9/10 | Risk: medium (inventory correctness; the rule itself is a product decision, not a code detail)
